News.title: Thousands more may be victims of sick forums where men give tips on drugging & raping women… amid warning of ‘epidemic’
News.content:
'TIP OF THE ICEBERG' Thousands more may be victims of sick forums where men give tips on drugging & raping women… amid warning of ‘epidemic’

TWISTED online forums where depraved men share tips of how to drug and rape women are going under the radar – sparking fears there may be thousands more victims who do not even know they are being targeted.

Not only are these forums affecting the UK, but they are also operating on a “truly international” level. Here, charities and survivors tell The Sun that use of these platforms, where men discuss how to sexually assault women and share abuse material, has become an “epidemic” – and the current statistics are just the “tip of the iceberg”.



In these warped groups, men ask strangers to come over and rape their own trusted long-term partners, the National Crime Agency has revealed.

The NCA pointed to the Gisèle Pelicot case as a shocking example of the depraved abuse these forums are capable of organising.



The survivor’s ex-husband, Dominique Pelicot, was jailed for 20 years for drugging, raping, and allowing dozens of other men to rape her while she was unconscious. He and 50 other men were found guilty of rape or sexual offences after the terrifying campaign of sexual abuse.

Pelicot’s story has been compared to that of Zoe Watts – whose husband is serving an 11-year sentence for drug-facilitated rape over 18 years of their relationship.

She told The Sun that forums where men discuss how to sexually assault women and share abuse material have become an “epidemic”.

On these websites, sick perpetrators invite men to take part in rapes, give the best advice on how to sedate targets, and share footage of their horrific abuse.

Discussions include sharing tactics to avoid being caught and requests for certain sexual attacks to be filmed.

Many victims do not even know they have been subjected to some of these heinous crimes, the NCA said.



Zoe, who was drugged, raped, and filmed for years in a horrific campaign of abuse, said the latest report was just the tip of the iceberg.

She said investigators were “very far behind the curve” as “thousands” of women are probably being sexually assaulted everyday without knowing.

Fears are mounting that the recently uncovered networks are just a small visible portion of the problem.



Zoe, 43, told us: “There are hundreds and thousands of women, I suspect, out there that are being sexually assaulted and they don’t know it.”

She said the lack of moderation on these warped websites is something relied upon by predators.

“Men are banking on us not finding out – they’re relying on our symptoms not being spotted,” she said.

“They’re relying on poor policing, they’re relying on shoddy internet and hosting regulations to continue to facilitate sexual assaults. These platforms aren’t being monitored correctly and there’s all this information and detail about how to carry out these acts.

“We’re basically letting it go on there in its hundreds and then trying to bring it down… it needs to be an offence to even have it uploaded.”



Zoe added: “It’s an epidemic, and it’s incredibly scary. Just speaking from my own experience, the sexual assaults, the drugs… it would have been over a nine-year period. I can’t imagine… how many other women are experiencing that.”

The activist, who started End Eye Check as a survivor-led campaign building awareness around the issue, has worked with several victims of disturbing online forums.

She explained: “I’ve got women involved in the campaign that are actively looking for themselves online because they know that a rape has happened and their partner won’t tell them where they are.



“It’s definitely a problem that’s increasing… I’ve got a lady involved in the campaign who’s in her 70s. It doesn’t discriminate by age, by gender, by social standing, by race – and that’s what’s scary.”

More than 270 suspects linked to one forum were identified by the NCA in their latest probe.

The agency informed police in several countries, with more than 90 per cent of the cases being sent abroad – highlighting the international scale of these groups.

In the UK, the probe has resulted in at least 14 investigations, with eight victim-survivors safeguarded.

It comes after the discovery of Telegram group in Germany that allegedly posed as a driving school, but was actually a cesspit where men bragged about raping women and shared assault strategies, prosecutors said.



Referring to women as “cars, sedatives as “fuel” and rape as “driving” three Chinese members of the group have been convicted while another is currently on trial in Berlin.

The case sent shock waves across Germany and China – and underscored the global scale of the problem.

Asked if she was scared by the prospect of predators coming to the UK to commit crimes before fleeing the country, Zoe said: “Absolutely.”

“The thing with the online platforms is it makes the availability, the access to a woman’s body so much more broader,” she said.



“These platforms have allowed a global network access to somebody who is like-minded, and wants to execute the attack.

“It is happening in 22 different countries… I think that realistically, these women are at risk anywhere… all you’ve got to do is hop on a plane really.”

Zoe added: “I think we’re dramatically underestimating the problem and the effect that it is having, because it’s committed on the whole by ‘nice men’.

“The facade of these men are, to the face of the public, all very lovely. You wouldn’t expect it.”

Rape Crisis England and Wales told The Sun it was a “deeply concerning phenomenon”.



They told us: “Some people may now be questioning whether something similar could have happened to them, or someone they know.

“We would encourage anyone who is worried or affected to seek support, including through the Rape Crisis 24/7 Support Line.”

The charity said the problem was getting worse due to the increase of readily available violent sexual material online.

“Many of these online platforms are reported to enable the sharing of advice, encouragement, and methods for carrying out sexual abuse without detection,” the organisation said.

“When we think about this as a growing problem online, we need to remember that platforms don’t exist in isolation.



“They exist within an online culture where increasingly extreme and violent sexual material is easily accessible, and where violence against women is amplified and rewarded.”

They said research demonstrated a “clear link between pornography use – particularly violent pornography – and harmful attitudes towards women”.

Because some of these networks are international, investigations can be “more complex” due to law enforcement agencies needing to coordinate across countries.

Nigel Leary, the deputy director of the NCA, said: “We believe we have uncovered a truly international network with group members identified in dozens of countries spanning every continent.

“In many of the cases we’ve seen so far, individuals have become victims of sexual assault crimes while sedated.”



The “most heinous sexual abuse” is being discussed on these forums, Leary added.

Rape Crisis CEO Ciara Bergman said the discovery was “alarming”.

She said: “Sadly, though, they are not surprising – these abuses are rooted in the same misogyny and objectification which underpin violence against women and girls the world over.

“We mustn’t forget that many of these abuses were filmed, shared and viewed by others on these forums. Online platforms have been allowed to profit from extremist acts of violence against women and girls for far too long.

“For many survivors, this news will be extraordinarily frightening and confusing.



“Many women will now be asking themselves whether they could have been affected, whether they can trust those closest to them, and what that will mean for them.

“To anyone reading this who is worried that they, or someone they know, may have experienced drug-facilitated sexual assault or rape: you do not have to go through this alone.”

News.title: Cops find body in woods after man ‘attacked at house’ 40 miles away as two arrested over ‘murder’
News.content:
'MURDER PROBE' Cops find body in woods after man ‘attacked at house’ 40 miles away as two arrested over ‘murder’

COPS have discovered a body in a woodland after two men were arrested on suspicion of murder.

Police received reports of an alleged attack at a property on Kingfisher Court in Wimbledon on Thursday July 9 at around 10.55pm.

Officers found no one at the address but suspected someone had been harmed and launched a probe.



The suspects, aged 27 and 32, turned themselves in at Medway Police Station in Gillingham Kent on Friday 10 July, the Met was informed.



The two men were arrested on suspicion of murder and remain in custody.

A third man was also arrested on suspicion of assisting an offender and has since been released on bail.

Cops visited a wooded area in Borstal, Kent, later on Friday and discovered the body of a man.

The victim has not yet been formally identified but officers believe they know who he is and have contacted his next-of-kin.

Detective Inspector Ben Dalloway said: “Our thoughts remain with the victim’s family who are understandably distraught at their loss. We will continue to offer them every support.

“This has been a fast-moving investigation and we are working tirelessly to establish the exact circumstances of the incident.

“Although we have made two arrests and do not believe there is any wider risk to the public, we would ask that anyone with information comes forward to police as soon as possible by calling 101 with CAD 9504/9JUL.”

News.title: We were sold dream but idyllic new estate has already been ‘abandoned’… it looks like it’s been hit by an earthquake
News.content:
ESTATE OF REPAIR We were sold dream but idyllic new estate has already been ‘abandoned’… it looks like it’s been hit by an earthquake

FURIOUS residents living on an idyllic estate have slammed developers after being promised wildflower meadows – but ended up with a jungle of 3ft weeds and paths that look like they’ve been struck by an earthquake.

Work started on the 79 new build property development, Nightingale View, within the village of Hamstreet, near Ashford, Kent, nearly three years ago before it opened in 2024.



The estimated £400,000 to £550,000 homes were marketed with a countryside feel overlooking fields.

But residents claim landscaping has been virtually non-existent – with out-of-control weeds growing where flowers should be, and tree saplings planted having already given up and died.



Meanwhile, the tarmac paths have cracked – leaving the feel of a ghost town after a natural disaster has struck.

And they argue tarmac footpath cracks have left some weeds growing 3ft high.



The site also boasts an 11-a-side grass football pitch which has hardly been used and a large pond which appears overgrown.

Residents say they have taken to cutting the grass areas themselves to keep them tidy – but wonder what exactly their maintenance fees are covering.



The concerns have led Ashford Borough Council to investigate whether any breaches of the planning permission have occurred.

Nightingale View was first built by Bovis, part of the Vistry Group, but maintenance has been handed over to new company Gateway.

But residents who originally paid £245 annually for services have now been given an annual estimated service charge – including ground maintenance – of £605.56p due from October.



Marion Jolin, 76, a retired GP receptionist, has lived on the estate with husband Cliff, 77, for just over two years.

The grandmother-of-one told The Sun: “Look at the state of it, I mean it’s dreadful.

“We’re supposed to have bulb planting and wild flowers, there’s supposed to be seating area where residents can meet up but that’s not appeared.



“We’ve been taken for mugs really. We’re all quite put out about it.”

The couple, who bought their house for £550,000, added: “They just haven’t maintained anything. It is frustrating.”

Alan Brown, 64, and wife Anne, 69, moved from North Ayrshire in Scotland to the Nightingale View estate in September 2023 to be close to their two grandchildren.

Alan said: “Even before we bought the house, we were given a map called the landscape master plan and it looked lovely.

“I know it’s an artist’s impression, but it had terms like an ‘avenue of trees’ – it said it would all be landscaped, short grass and in the middle of the grass there would be bulbs, that’s the verges.



“Some of the grass would have what they called meadow wildflowers.

“None of that has been put in.”

He said a lot of the site was weeds, mainly ox tongue.



Alan added: “There’s anger here. I am angry that we’ve come here and we were promised and that it would be a pleasant, ecologically friendly area to live and it’s not.”

Another resident Dan Cheshire, 37, said: “We were told there was going to be this and that, and they’ve just not delivered on the majority of it, really.

“We have a tree in the front lawn, and it was planted at an angle, and it’s forever gone further and further over.

“Everything is pretty much dead. Even the back garden. I’ve been in battle with them to relay the back garden.

“When we moved in it was all green, then it turned to mud. They re-turfed it, and now it’s all mud again – because they haven’t put the foundations in for it to grow.



“Across the drive from us that’s meant to be a wildflower meadow, it’s just weeds.”

Sharon Guilfoyle, 60, who has lived on the development for 15 months, said: “The landscaping is appalling. The tarmac paths have cracked.

“We reported the path, but nothing. Next door have had their garden done two or three times.

“The gardens are not good.”

But bucking the trent somewhat, Egas Pinto Basco, 37, a video game developer, has lived on the estate for a year and does not seem to have the same complaints.



He said: “I do see them mowing the grass every now and then, every few months or so. I saw them once re-seeding the grass itself, only once.

“I think it’s fine. I’ve moved here from London where no one cares – people care here more.”

A council spokesperson said: “We are aware of some of the landscaping issues raised concerning the development at Nightingale View and are currently investigating them to determine if any planning breaches have occurred.”

A Vistry spokesperson said: “We recognise that some residents at Nightingale View are disappointed with the landscaping, and we are sorry it has not yet met expectations.

“Vistry will fund all necessary remediation, including replacing any dead or missing trees and resolving wider landscaping issues, and residents will not be asked to cover these costs.



“While day-to-day management has transferred to Gateway, we remain responsible for putting things right and are focused on bringing the development up to the intended standard.”

A spokesperson for Gateway said: “Gateway has been managing Nightingale View on behalf of Nightingale View (Hamstreet) Management Company Limited since 8th May 2026.

“Since our appointment, we have been working closely with both residents and the developer to address the concerns raised.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“We can confirm that remedial works will be carried out on behalf of the developer to rectify specific issues on the estate, including the cracked tarmac.

“These works will be funded by the developer and will therefore be at no additional cost to residents.”

News.title: Supermarket worker held hostage by shopper ‘armed with knife’ in Berlin for 11 HOURS as cops finally swoop on suspect
News.content:
A SUPERMARKET worker was held hostage for 11 hours by a shopper who was reportedly armed with a huge knife.

Cops swooped on the suspect Saturday morning and freed the hostage after a tense stand-off.



She had been trapped in a shop in Berlin since late on Friday night after a suspect brandished a “very big” knife at the checkout, a witness said.

Elijah, 22, said the woman “was simply in the wrong place at the wrong time” when the suspect pulled out a weapon shortly before closing time.



He told Bild: “The perpetrator was at the checkout, refused to put the items on the conveyor belt, and then suddenly pulled out a knife.

“It was definitely a large knife, a shiny knife.”

Elijah said he ran out of the shop and called the cops.

Police were seen climbing ladders and peering into the shop overnight to try and talk the hostage-taker down.

But he refused to negotiate and cops ended the stand-off by force.

The woman was freed in a dramatic operation on Saturday morning after the agonising 11-hour wait.



She was taken to safety but is in shock after the ordeal, police said.

Police stormed the supermarket around 9.20am.

They had surrounded the shop with special units, including SWAT teams and dog handlers.



A SWAT team took the hostage-taker down after reportedly tasering him.

The suspect was seen being taken away on a stretcher with minor injuries after police overpowered him inside the shop.

He did not know his alleged victim, Bild reported.

Police spokesman Florian Nath told reporters: “Special forces were able to overpower the perpetrator and free the woman being held captive.”

All other staff members who were in the shop when the suspect showed the knife managed to escape unharmed.



The high-stakes stand-off comes after a police officer was injured in a hostage situation in Baltimore in March.

Police responded to a burglary call and were “immediately met with gunfire”.

The suspect was shooting from inside of a house when an officer was shot in the leg, Police Commissioner Richard Worley told reporters.

One victim jumped out of a window in the home in an attempt to flee, injuring herself, police said.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The suspect held another hostage, at one point holding a gun to the second victim’s head, police said.



SWAT authorities arrived on the scene, and the suspect was killed by a sniper, Worley confirmed.

News.title: At least 15 killed after tourist boat capsizes on day trip to Vietnam island leaving passengers trapped inside
News.content:
BOAT TRAGEDY At least 15 killed after tourist boat capsizes on day trip to Vietnam island leaving passengers trapped inside

A PACKED tourist boat has capsized while returning from a day trip in Vietnam leaving at least 15 dead.

The vessel had been carrying 32 holidaymakers from India and four crew members when it suddenly flipped and threw everyone overboard.



The tourists had been on an island-hopping day trip from Hon May Rut Ngoai when their speedboat overturned 1,310ft from Phu Quoc.

Nearby tourist boats raced to the scene after spotting the capsized vessel at around around 1pm on Saturday.



Crew members desperately pulled passengers from the water.

One boat owner – who arrived around five minutes after the boat capsized – said: “Only a few people were brought out conscious.”



He added that the water had been choppy at the time and that the high number of people trapped inside the boat made rescue efforts difficult.

Border guards and navy eventually saved 21 people but 15 people – two women and 13 men – were confirmed dead.

All of the 15 bodies were recovered and the injured have been rushed to hospital.



In a post on X the Indian Embassy in Vietnam described the incident as “tragic”.

They added: “Exact details of the incident ​are being ascertained as search and ​rescue operations by local authorities are ongoing.”

The cause of the capsizing is not yet clear and investigators have launched a probe into the fatal incident.

The Indian Embassy have launched two control rooms to assist family and loved ones affected by the deadly accident.



Officials have reportedly confirmed that five tourists from Andhra Pradesh and 17 from Tamil Nadu were among those on board.

Of these, two are safe and well and the rest have been hospitalised.

And Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi has said that the passengers were taking part in an annual meeting of a private mobile phone company.

He added that officials from the Indian Embassy were on the scene.

The speedboat was hopping between two islands famed for their white sand beaches and crystal clear waters, attracting millions of visitors a year.

News.title: Four teenagers charged with 12 counts of rape after woman ‘sexually assaulted at house’
News.content:
'RAPE' PROBE Four teenagers charged with 12 counts of rape after woman ‘sexually assaulted at house’

FOUR teenagers have been charged with 12 counts of rape after a woman was allegedly assaulted at a house in a seaside town.

Detectives made the arrests after receiving a report the victim was being threatened and raped at a property in Weston-super-Mare, Somerset, on June 21.

The investigation was undertaken by Operation Bluestone, a specialist sexual offences team at Avon and Somerset Police.

Tommy Campebell, 19, has been charged with six counts of rape, one count of sexual assault, one count of false imprisonment and one count of assault causing actual bodily harm.





Rio Welling, 18, has been charged with two counts of rape and one count of false imprisonment.

A 17-year-old boy, who cannot be named because of his age, has been charged with three counts of rape, one count of false imprisonment, and one count of assault causing actual bodily harm.

A second 17-year-old boy, who cannot be named because of his age, has been charged with one count of rape, and one count of assault causing actual bodily harm.

They were all remanded in custody to appear at Taunton Magistrates’ Court later today (July 11).

Detective Inspector Natalie Thatcher said: “Our investigation into this incredibly serious incident has been taking place over the past few weeks and the charges authorised by the Crown Prosecution Service are a significant milestone.

“The victim has been updated by specially trained officers who will continue to provide her with as much support as she needs.

“We are aware the co-ordinated pre-planned arrest attempts across Weston and Worle on Thursday did cause some local concern, which is why we wanted to be transparent around why they were necessary.

“We would like to thank people for their patience while those enquiries were carried out.”

News.title: Putin is tightening stranglehold on Belarus & blackmailing Europe – I know truth about nuke threats, says exiled leader
News.content:
VLADIMIR Putin is tightening his grip on Belarus and blackmailing Europe with nuclear threats, the country’s exiled opposition leader has warned.

Moscow is deliberately exploiting fear and uncertainty in a bid to pressure Nato and destabilise Europe, Sviatlana Tsikhanouskaya said in a exclusive interview with The Sun.



The warning comes after Russia and Belarus held their first-ever joint nuclear exercises in May – overseen by Putin and Belarusian leader Alexander Lukashenko.

Putin has previously claimed the Kremlin deployed nuclear weapons to Belarus in 2023, as tensions with Nato escalated over the war in Ukraine.



Tsikhanouskaya, who lives in exile in Lithuania after a disputed presidential election in which she challenged Lukashenko, said: “Russia is deliberately using nuclear ambiguity as a tool of intimidation and blackmail.

“The goal is to create fear and uncertainty among Ukraine, Nato, and Belarus’ neighbours.”



Revealing the truth about Putin’s nuclear war-mongering, she said it is a crafted strategy designed to appear confusing and ambiguous.

“The Kremlin wants the West to hesitate, Ukraine to feel threatened from the north, and European societies to worry about escalation,” she said.



At the centre of her warning is Belarus, a country of 9.5million people, which she says is being turned into an extension of Vlad’s war machine.

Lukashenko’s rule has increasingly been described by Western analysts as that of a Kremlin-aligned strongman, presiding over a Russian “puppet state”.

“Belarus is already being transformed into a permanent military platform for Russia,” Tsikhanouskaya said.

The deployment of Russian nuclear weapons and military infrastructure inside Belarus has removed any meaningful sense of sovereignty from Minsk, she added.

“In reality, they make Belarus less secure and less sovereign,” she said.



“Decisions about these weapons are not made in Minsk – they are made in Moscow.”

Belarus is no longer a bystander to the conflict in Ukraine, but an active component of Russia’s war effort, she explained.

“Russia is systematically expanding its military presence in Belarus,” she said.



“It deploys military infrastructure, missiles, and troops.”

Analysts have warned Belarus could be used by Moscow to cut off key military supply routes in western Ukraine in the event of escalation.

What is emerging, she argued, is a deeply embedded system supporting Russia’s military operations.

“More than 500 Belarusian enterprises are involved in supporting Russia’s military industry in one way or another,” she revealed.

“Belarusian factories produce components, repair equipment, and supply goods needed for the Russian war effort.”



Tsikhanouskaya pointed to the presence of Russian military infrastructure, missile systems, and facilities inside Belarus – including systems that support drone operations against Ukraine.

“We know about transmitters and relay systems near the Belarusian-Ukrainian border that help Russian drones navigate and strike targets inside Ukraine,” she said.

Despite these developments, Tsikhanouskaya said she does not believe Belarusian troops are likely to be directly deployed into Ukraine any time soon.

“I do not believe the direct involvement of Belarusian troops is likely,” she said.

Instead, she said Russia is using Belarus primarily as a base of operations.



“Today, Russia does not need Belarusian soldiers as much as it needs Belarusian territory, infrastructure, military production, logistics, and political control,” she said.

Belarus has become indispensable to Moscow’s regional military might Tsikhanouskaya said.

“Without Belarus, many of Putin’s imperial ambitions would be much harder to realise,” she explained.



Inside Belarus, she said, the public is strongly opposed to involvement in the war.

A poll suggested around one in four Belarusians supports Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, while another survey found just 2 per cent would support sending Belarusian troops into combat.

“The good news is that most Belarusians do not want this war,” she said.

“They do not see Ukrainians as enemies. There is a strong anti-war consensus in society.”

Tsikhanouskaya said this is widespread across society.



“Belarusians do not share Russia’s imperial ambitions,” she said.

“The Belarusian army itself is not eager to fight.

“Many have relatives, friends, or personal ties in Ukraine. They know the human cost of this war.”



For Tsikhanouskaya, the resistance is one of the main reasons Belarus has not yet entered the war directly.

She argued the current leadership is constrained not only by Moscow, but by the memory of past unrest.

“The regime barely survived the 2020 protests and understands that repression has not changed people’s views,” she said.

Tsikhanouskaya highlighted the potential for resistance within Belarusian society if escalation were attempted.

“The regime may control people through fear, but fear is not the same as loyalty,” she said.



She pointed to acts of sabotage and disruption that followed Russia’s invasion of Ukraine as evidence of underlying resistance.

She said: “We saw dozens of acts of railway sabotage that disrupted Russian military logistics. Thousands of people shared information about Russian troop movements.”

According to Tsikhanouskaya, this pattern reflects a deeper reality inside Belarus: opposition to the war is widespread, even if it is not always visible.

“The overwhelming majority do not want Belarus to enter this war,” she said. “Support for Lukashenka and for Russia’s aggression is very low.”

Even under repression, she said, many Belarusians continue to resist in quieter ways.



“Many others support Ukraine through humanitarian work, medical assistance, information sharing, and cyber resistance”, Tsikhanouskaya said.

Taking aim at the leadership in Minsk, Tsikhanouskaya described Lukashenka as increasingly dependent on Putin.

“He survived only because Putin kept him in power,” she said, referring to the aftermath of the disputed 2020 election.

And the relationship between the two leaders has become practically inseparable.

“Today, it is impossible to separate Lukashenka from Putin,” she said.



“Putin keeps Lukashenka in power, and Lukashenka serves Putin’s interests.

“The weaker Lukashenka becomes, the weaker Putin becomes too – and vice versa.”

She rejected suggestions the Belarusian leader could be brought back on board.

“Our goal is not to save Lukashenko. Our goal is to save Belarus from both Lukashenka and Putin,” she said.

For her, the only path forward is political change inside Belarus itself.



“The only real solution is democratic change in Belarus,” she said.

“We need to dismantle the pro-Russian dictatorship, restore Belarusian sovereignty, and allow Belarusians to choose their future through free and fair elections.

“A few years ago this may have seemed impossible. Today, we see that a new window of opportunity may be opening.”

Tsikhanouskaya said international leaders should focus on preventing escalation – particularly through sanctions and diplomatic pressure.

“Sometimes I feel the world still does not fully understand,” she said.



“What Putin is doing to Belarus is also a war – not with tanks, but through military control, political pressure, and the gradual destruction of Belarusian sovereignty.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

In a direct plea to Belarusian soldiers and citizens, she said: “Ukraine is not your enemy. Do not become instruments of Putin’s war. This is not only important for Belarus.

“It is important for Ukraine, for regional security, and for the future of Europe.”

News.title: Devastating aftermath of Spain’s deadly wildfire after victims die fleeing along riverbed ‘trap’ as missing Brit found
News.content:
DEVASTATING photos reveal the blackened hilltops of southern Spain ravaged by one of the country’s deadliest wildfires – as heartbreaking details of escape attempts emerge.

At least 12 people have been killed after some died trying to flee by running down a dry riverbed – which turned out to be a fatal “trap”.



A Brit who was reported missing during the wildfire has been found “alive and okay”, according to her family.

Haunting pictures emerged of the gutted vehicle four British nationals are believed to have died in after they were trapped by flames as they tried to evacuate the area.





Horrifying photos showed blackened trees standing starkly on the devastated hilltops of Almería – surrounded by scorched grasses.

More than 16,000 acres have been burned to the ground and 1,448 people have been evacuated.

The fires continued to blaze into the early hours – as more than 500 firefighters and eight aircrafts battle the flames.

The wildfires have been some of the worst that Spain has ever seen – killing 12 people with more feared dead, including children.



A further eight people have been hospitalised – with four in serious condition – and 20 people are missing.

Four Brits are feared to have died while trying to flee the inferno at Los Gallardos – after choosing a deadly escape route.

They drove down a dry riverbed – which turned out to be a deadly “trap”, according to Antonio Sanz, the minister for health and emergencies in the region.



Dry vegetation was the “perfect fuel that, combined with the wind, becomes a ticking time bomb”, added regional president Juanma Moreno.

Seven others were killed in the same spot while trying to escape on foot.

In a subsequent press address, Sanz said the seven people on foot could also include British nationals.

Bedar’s mayor Angel Francisco Collado Fernandez added yesterday afternoon referencing the group of nine: “We insisted to the people that didn’t want to leave that they had to do so.

“Fortunately one of those who decided to stay is still alive, recommending that the other nine neighbours take refuge in his home.



“They didn’t take his advice and seven died and the other two suffered serious burns and are on their way to the Virgen del Rocio Hospital in Seville.”

Regional president Moreno said the blaze was caused by a downed power cable which broke and ignited in the ditch – but the power company has denied that the cable sparked the fire.

At least 1,405 have been evacuated from their homes as dramatic photos show hellish flames snaking across the hills to residential buildings.



Patricia McGough had launched a desperate appeal for her daughter Jada after she disappeared near the blazing inferno.

She shared a photo of her daughter with her pet dog on Facebook, saying: “My daughter is missing. She was driving a red Ford Fiesta and had her dog with her. Has anyone seen her?”

The woman was found on Saturday – and Patricia shared her relief with The Sun.

She said: “She has been found. She’s ok.”

Victims are thought to be made up of 10 foreign nationals, likely Brits and Belgians, and two Spanish locals.



At least eight of the dead are believed to be retired expats, with three feared to be children and one a cyclist, local media reported.

The area is hugely popular with Brit retirees and expats.

Authorities have been unable to identify the bodies due to their severe burns and are reportedly struggling to work out the gender of some victims.

Brit Patricia Garlic, 78, described the moment she first spotted the fire – and authorities begged them to flee.

She saw a huge plume of smoke on the horizon and “a fire by the roadside”.



“They gave us ten minutes to grab the essentials”, she recounted, adding “we were scared because we didn’t know what was going to happen.”

Liz Fowles, 52, from Birmingham, saw a haze of smoke blocking the sun.

“We thought it was just sand”, she said – but when she saw the fire on the mountains, she immediately packed her bags to flee.

Uriel Carbonell and Mariana Rodríguez, both 18, returned to their grandmother’s home in the heart of the fires at Bédar.

They arrived to find the air thick with smoke, saying ” we could barely breathe”.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

They didn’t even enter the home – pausing only to grab their grandma’s two dogs Bimba and Lola before fleeing the scene.

“The fire was already very close,” they recounted, adding “cats, chickens, turtles… were left behind. We don’t know what happened to them”.

News.title: Four teens charged with 12 counts of rape after woman 'imprisoned' in home
News.content:
Four teens charged with 12 counts of rape after woman 'imprisoned' in home

Officers have arrested and charged four men in connection with a rape - all aged in their teens - after a woman was reportedly held against her will at an address

View Image The force confirmed the four teens have been arrested and charged (Image: Getty Images)

A group of four teenagers have been charged in connection with a serious rape investigation after a woman was allegedly sexually assaulted at a home in Weston-Super-Mare.

The four young men, aged 19, 18 and two 17 year olds, have been arrested and charged after Avon and Somerset Police launched a specialist investigation into a serious sexual offence.

A woman was reportedly threatened and raped at a property on Sunday, June 21, where it is alleged she was kept 'imprisoned' during the attack.

Tommy Campbell, 19, from Weston-Super-Mare, has been charged with six counts of rape, one count of sexual assault, one count of false imprisonment, and one count of assault causing actual bodily harm.

Rio Welling, 18, from Weston-Super-Mare, has been charged with two counts of rape and one count of false imprisonment.

Due to legal reasons, the 17-year-old boys cannot be named because of their age. One has been charged with three counts of rape, one count of false imprisonment, and one count of assault causing actual bodily harm. The other 17-year-old has been charged with one count of rape, and one count of assault causing actual bodily harm.

All four were remanded in custody to appear at Taunton Magistrates’ Court later today (11 July).

Detective Inspector Natalie Thatcher said: “Our investigation into this incredibly serious incident has been taking place over the past few weeks and the charges authorised by the Crown Prosecution Service are a significant milestone.

Article continues below

“The victim has been updated by specially trained officers who will continue to provide her with as much support as she needs.

“We are aware the co-ordinated pre-planned arrest attempts across Weston and Worle on Thursday did cause some local concern, which is why we wanted to be transparent around why they were necessary. We would like to thank people for their patience while those enquiries were carried out.”

News.title: Ann Widdecombe murder probe: Manhunt resumes as police focus on mystery of 29 missing minutes
News.content:
Devon and Cornwall Police launched a murder probe after ex-Conservative MP and Brexit Party MEP Ann Widdecombe was found dead inside her home with "serious injuries", with a man arrested but later released

A manhunt has resumed for the killer of former MP and MEP Ann Widdecombe after a 26-year-old man arrested on suspicion of murder was released.

Devon and Cornwall Police said the individual had left custody and is no longer part of the investigation. Police said they remained "open-minded" about the probe, and had no information to believe Ms Widdecombe's death was politically motivated.

Detectives are continuing to piece together the events surrounding the politician's sudden death, with mystery over her movements after she failed to show for a scheduled TV engagement on Wednesday morning but then apparently sent a message later regarding another appearance.

Concerns were raised when she failed to respond to follow-up messages, ultimately leading to the discovery of the 78-year-old's body at her home in Haytor, Devon. Police are trying to establish what took place in the 29 minutes between Ms Widdecome's final contact and the later message to her which went unanswered.

The long-time Tory switched allegiance to the Brexit Party in 2019, and then to Reform UK. She had lived alone in Haytor since retiring as the MP for Maidstone and The Weald in 2010.

News.title: Wimbledon winner looks unrecognisable now 22 years after winning title
News.content:
Wimbledon winner looks unrecognisable now 22 years after winning title

This ex-Wimbledon champion still stuns fans with her dramatic makeover since retiring from tennis in 2020, swapping her blonde locks for a brunette look

View 3 Images Former Wimbledon champion Maria Sharapova has been dubbed "unrecognisable" (Image: Getty)

Former Wimbledon champion Maria Sharapova continues to leave fans gobsmacked after unveiling a dramatic new look in retirement. The 39-year-old brought her professional career to an end in 2020 and is now barely recognisable, having swapped out her trademark blonde hair.

‌



Sharapova first shot to fame as a teenager when she defeated Serena Williams at SW19 in 2004. This was a victory that became almost as iconic as her flowing blonde locks.

‌



Yet since calling time on her playing days, the sporting icon has ditched her celebrated image in favour of a sleek brunette style, leaving supporters speechless and branding her "unrecognisable."

‌



The bold new look first turned heads when she debuted it at an event in Italy. Sharapova, pictured alongside her British partner Alex Gilkes, caught the eye at the Hotel II Pellicano's 60th anniversary celebration in Monte Argentario.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

Wimbledon host Isa Guha's replacement confirmed as BBC star steps in READ MORE :

John McEnroe shows true colours with comment about Emma Raducanu READ MORE :

During her illustrious playing career, Sharapova claimed all four Grand Slam titles, kicking things off with her breakthrough triumph at Wimbledon, before going on to lift the US Open trophy in 2006.

‌



View 3 Images Sharapova became renowned for her blonde style (Image: Getty)

The Russian star then conquered the Australian Open in 2008 and added the French Open to her collection in both 2012 and 2014, while also reaching the final in 2013. Alongside her Grand Slam haul, Sharapova also pocketed an Olympic silver medal at the London Games in 2012, narrowly losing out to Williams in the women's singles final.

Sharapova not only became the third-youngest woman to triumph at Wimbledon but also cemented her place in the history books as the first Russian to complete a career Grand Slam.

‌



Her accomplishments weren't confined to smashing balls on the court, as she also carved out a remarkable path beyond it. Forbes featured her on their esteemed list as one of the top 100 most powerful celebrities worldwide from 2005 to 2011.

That said, it wasn't all plain sailing. In 2016, Sharapova encountered turbulence when she received a 15-month ban (initially two years) following a positive test for meldonium.

View 3 Images The Russian star wows fans with her transformation (Image: Getty)

‌



She acknowledged the violation but maintained it was an inadvertent error, explaining she'd been following her doctor's guidance and was oblivious to the fact the substance had been added to WADA's banned list. Since retiring from tennis, Sharapova has been living the dream, enjoying lavish getaways with her fiance Gilkes, who got down on one knee in 2020.

In 2022, the pair welcomed their first child, Theodore, and Sharapova's Instagram now proudly displays 'Mama' in her profile. The former SW19 winner, who's amassed a substantial £31million in prize money, has thrived in the business world too, launching her confectionery brand Sugarpova and supporting sunscreen giants Supergoop during her playing days.

Since retiring from the sport, however, she has considerably expanded her business empire, throwing her weight behind wellness giant Therabody and securing a seat on the board of high-end fashion label Moncler in 2022. Sharapova also acts as a consultant to Naked Retail and Bright, whilst holding stakes in a number of other enterprises including UFC and Tonal.

News.title: Spain wildfires live: 12 dead in Almeria 'including Brits' near expat village
News.content:
Twelve people have been killed in a wildfire in Los Gallardos, Almería, Spain - at least four of the dead are thought to be British and were found in a burnt out car

FOUR Brits 'feared DEAD in Spain' after burnt out car found in WILDFIRE in Los Gallardos

Several Brits are feared to have died in a wildfire in Spain which has claimed 12 lives. Local reports suggest three of the dead are children.

Officials said four people found dead in a burned out car in Los Gallardos, Almería are believed to be British. There are also fears that Brits could be among a group of people found dead while trying to escape the flames on foot.

Witnesses say the wildfire was caused by a downed power line. Around 150 firefighters have been deployed to tackle the fire in a village called Bedar, alongside military personnel.

A source said the village is made up of roughly 70 per cent British inhabitants, most of whom are elderly and retired there.

Three days of mourning have been declared to remember those whose lives were lost in the fire.

News.title: Prince Harry live: King Charles 'putting strain on relationship' with William in meeting Harry, Meghan and kids
News.content:
Prince Harry finally ensured King Charles got to meet his grandchildren for the first time in four years on a family visit to Highgrove, but Jennie Bond says not everyone will be thrilled

The King may have inadvertently 'put strain' on his excellent relationship with Prince William by reuniting with the Duke and Duchess of Sussex and their children, it is feared.

Charles welcomed Prince Harry's family to his Highgrove residence yesterday afternoon after days of speculation over whether the family meeting would take place. Archie, seven, and Lilibet, five, last saw their grandfather in person during Queen Elizabeth II’s Platinum Jubilee celebrations in 2022.

It is understood the Queen who has a private home near to the King’s Gloucestershire property was also among the group. The meeting between Charles and the young prince and princess is likely to be interpreted as a sign of the thawing of the relationship between the King and his son Harry.

But royal expert Jennie Bond worries it could do harm, with William still deeply hurt by his brother's actions against the Firm.

Harry's rift with William is ongoing however and shows no sign of abating and the family reunion took place during the same afternoon William was playing in a charity polo match at Windsor.

In February 2024 Harry made a transatlantic dash from his Californian home to Britain to see his father following his cancer diagnosis, which may have led to the first steps in a reconciliation between the pair.

Harry had planned to bring his family to the UK while he undertook a week-long series of events promoting charities and organisations close to his heart including the Invictus Games he founded. Security issues prevented Meghan and the children travelling with him on Monday but it appears concerns over safety were mitigated to allow the visit to Highgrove to take place.

The Mirror exclusively reported this week the monarch, 77, instructed senior aides to engage in ongoing talks with the Duke and Duchess of Sussex, to secure time in his busy diary around his public duties.

Within hours of Prince Harry's solo Invictus Games event drawing to a close in Birmingham, Princess Kate stepped out to support her husband Prince William.
